The 12h MHC Class I Transient Peak: A Shared Antiviral/Immune Module

The most striking cross-pathway finding is the **identical transient-peak profile of MHC class I genes (H2-K1, H2-Q1, H2-Q2, H2-Bl, H2-Q4, H2-D1)** peaking at +2.65 at 12h across four distinct viral-infection pathways: HSV-1 [1], HTLV-1 [4], HPV [6], and cellular senescence [13].

Bcl2 as a Central Pro-Survival Hub

**Bcl2 shows the most reproducible signal across the entire dataset**: monotonic upregulation from 1.51 to 3.06 by 24h, appearing in the apoptosis pathway [5], autophagy pathway [2], and AGE-RAGE signaling [9].
This module is also consistent with the senescence-associated immune response described in AUF1-driven senescence [3] and the immune surveillance role in papillomavirus-driven skin cancer [6,7].
